title: Table, pulpit, font
hookLine: where the furniture sits says what's central

lines: A TABLE, A PULPIT, A FONT.
cards: A table. A pulpit. A font.
Those three keep turning up in churches. In one church, the table stands in the middle at the front, candles on it, and the pulpit waits off to one side.
In another, a tall pulpit rises dead center, a big Bible open on it, and the table sits lower down, in front.
In a third, behind the pulpit, set high into the wall where everyone can see it, there's a pool of water deep enough to stand in. Three arrangements, and none of them by accident.

teach.b: Jesus says, "For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also." A church's floor plan is a little like that: where the furniture stands shows what the people treasure in their worship. Start with the table.
At the last supper, Jesus took bread and said, "This do in remembrance of me."

Catholic Christians call it an altar, Orthodox Christians the holy table or altar, and they place it at the heart of the church, because they understand the Eucharist celebrated there as the center of their worship.
Some Lutheran and Anglican churches do the same. Next, the pulpit.

teach.h: THE PULPIT: FAITH COMETH BY HEARING.
teach.b: Paul writes, "So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."
In Reformed and Presbyterian churches, the pulpit may stand at the center with the Bible open on it, because the word read and preached is where they hear God speak.
The table is still there, and honored, but the eye goes first to the open book.

teach.h: THE FONT: WATER IN FULL VIEW.
teach.b: Then, the font: water for baptism. In some Baptist churches the baptistry, a pool for full immersion, is set high behind the pulpit, so every baptism happens in front of the whole room.
Tomorrow, the font gets a day of its own. Last, all three together. Some churches set them in a line or a triangle, holding all three together.
Every arrangement answers the same question in wood and stone instead of words. Christians don't all give the same answer, and each answer can be read from the back pew.

how: Catholic and Orthodox churches place the altar at the center; some Reformed and Presbyterian churches center the pulpit and the open Bible; some Baptist churches set the baptistry where the whole congregation can see it; other churches balance all three.

games.q: you're helping plan a church for people who believe faith comes by hearing the word of God. what goes dead center?
o: the pulpit, with the Bible open on it
games.why: Reformed and Presbyterian churches may center the pulpit for just that reason: "faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."

practice: Let your eyes move around the room you're in without judging anything: what stands in the middle, and what do the chairs face, a table, a screen, a window? Rest your eyes on that center for a while.
If you pray, hold Jesus's words in mind, where your treasure is, there will your heart be also; or simply notice what the room has been built around.

wordCard.voice: Table. The Lord's table, the altar; with the pulpit and the font, one of three pieces whose places show what a church puts first.
